AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #5
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agricultural Biotechnology? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Agricultural Biotechnology.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Biotechnology.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agricultural Biotechnology.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agricultural Biotechnology.

4. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Health: Disease Control? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Health: Disease Control.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Health: Disease Control.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Health: Disease Control.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Disease Control.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

7. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Breeding? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Breeding.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Breeding.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Breeding.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Breeding.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Forage Crops? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Forage Crops.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Forage Crops.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Forage Crops.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Forage Crops.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Powered Agricultural Implements? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Powered Agricultural Implements.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Powered Agricultural Implements.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Powered Agricultural Implements.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Powered Agricultural Implements.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Cropping? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Cropping.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Cropping.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Cropping.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Cropping.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agri- business Accounts? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agri- business Accounts.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agri- business Accounts.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Agri- business Accounts.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agri- business Accounts.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Disease control? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Disease control.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Disease control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Disease control.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Disease control.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Livestock Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Livestock Nutrition.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Livestock Nutrition.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Livestock Nutrition.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Livestock Nutrition.

15. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

16. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Urban and peri-urban Agriculture? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.

18. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

19. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

20. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

21. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Erosion Control? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Erosion Control.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Erosion Control.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Erosion Control.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Erosion Control.

22. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
23. In three clear sentences, explain Business and Career Opportunities in Agriculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Soil Erosion Control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Ornamental Cropping and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

26. In three clear sentences, explain Crop Protection: Disease control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Forage Crops and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Livestock Nutrition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

29. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Breeding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

30. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Health: Disease Control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
